title: Biosecurity Amendment (No Crime to Return Home) Bill 2021
short_title: Biosecurity Amendment (No Crime to Return Home) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prevent the Health Minister using human biosecurity emergency powers to block Australian citizens and permanent residents overseas from returning to Australia.
It would restrict both emergency requirements and directions, and repeal the May 2021 travel-pause determination that barred arrivals who had recently been in India.
Other biosecurity measures could still apply after return, while permanent residents relying on the protection would need a valid Resident Return visa when arriving.
changes: Emergency determinations could no longer prevent or restrict covered people entering Australian territory.
The same limit would apply to the Minister's emergency directions.
The amendments would govern new requirements and directions during both existing and future emergency periods.
The legislation would commence the day after Royal Assent.
summary.affected: Australian citizens and permanent residents overseas, and the Health Minister exercising emergency biosecurity powers, are affected.
